item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Antidepressant

lookback_source.quote: N0415C1. Antidepressant: Check if an antidepressant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period; if the resident's admission/entry or reentry occurred less than 7 days before, the window is "since admission/entry or reentry." The manual uses "7-day look-back period" for the Column 1 (is taking) sub-item and "observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)" for the Column 2 (indication noted) sub-item; the Coding Instructions on p. N-6 describe Column 1 as the "7-day observation period." The document does not state how the days are counted relative to the ARD on the supplied pages.

coding_levels.label: Antidepressant — Column 1, Is taking (checked)
coding_levels.definition: Check if an antidepressant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415C1. Antidepressant: Check if an antidepressant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Antidepressant — Column 2, Indication noted (checked)
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all antidepressant medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415C2. Antidepressant: Check if there is an indication noted for all antidepressant medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 1 (N0415C1): check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (N0415C2) is coded only if Column 1 is checked; check Column 2 if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used (e.g., oxazepam prescribed as a hypnotic is coded as an antianxiety medication).

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification must be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how the medication is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications are coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination — e.g., a single tablet combining an antipsychotic and an antidepressant is coded in both the antipsychotic and antidepressant categories.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination. For example, if the resident receives a single tablet that combines an antipsychotic and an antidepressant, then both antipsychotic and antidepressant categories should be coded.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication only if the patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products are dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; use of the listed reference resources is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: The above resource list is not all-inclusive, and use of these resources is not required for MDS completion.

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that the medication was received by the resident and for the indication of its use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Stated as Step 1 for assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Stated as Step 2 for assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: The indication must be the identified, documented clinical rationale for administering the medication, based upon the physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding of pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0; facilities may wish to identify a consistently used classification resource.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish") but with an expectation that sources supporting coding are identifiable.

federal.criterion: When a resident receives medications in all three high-risk drug classes (antipsychotic, antianxiety, hypnotic) simultaneously there must be a clear clinical indication; adequate documentation is essential in justifying their use.

source.quote: Please note: if a resident is receiving medications in all three of these high-risk drug classes simultaneously there must be a clear clinical indication for the use of these medications.

federal.notes: Stated in the N0415 example note about antipsychotic/antianxiety/hypnotic combinations; not specific to the antidepressant class.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section N pages do not tie N0415C to any payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Window wording for the Column 2 (indication noted) sub-item versus the Column 1 (is taking) sub-item

positions.claim: N0415C1 uses the "7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)."

source.quote: N0415C1. Antidepressant: Check if an antidepressant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

positions.claim: N0415C2 uses "the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)" without stating a 7-day figure.

source.quote: N0415C2. Antidepressant: Check if there is an indication noted for all antidepressant medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

positions.claim: The N0415 Coding Instructions describe Column 1 as the "7-day observation period," using "observation period" and "look-back period" interchangeably.

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

conflicts.resolution: unresolved — surface to user; the manual appears to use "observation period" and "7-day look-back period" interchangeably for N0415, but never states this explicitly on the supplied pages.

common_audit_citations.notes: Cited by the manual as a source of additional information on psychoactive medications (which include antidepressants) and on common medication-medication interactions; not framed as an audit finding.
